recentItems.title: Will Putin REALLY GO THIS FAR? The Kremlin's crazy plan for a new mobilization REVEALED!
recentItems.description:
The Russian economy and aviation sector are feeling the mounting pressure of war and sanctions, but what could be the Kremlin's next move? Journalist Anna Danylchuk suggests that Putin might resort to a deliberate escalation against NATO to justify a new wave of mobilization and internal repression. In this interview, we also discuss the impact of Ukrainian drones, the crisis in Russian civil aviation, the possibility of a Kremlin coup, and the stances of China and India. Is Russia capable of changing after Putin, and what could actually force Moscow to end the war? Watch in this issue.

recentItems.title: Domino effect for Putin: burning refineries, a paralyzed Moscow, and Ukraine's fortified defense
recentItems.description:
Russia's oil infrastructure is under mounting pressure. Following Ukrainian strikes, Russia's second-largest oil refinery has ground to a halt, with attack ranges extending up to 1,900 km in August. Concurrently, Moscow airports are suffering major disruptions due to drones, while fuel shortages grip dozens of regions. The Kremlin is already budgeting for its worst oil production forecast in 17 years. Meanwhile, Russia is aiding Iran with missile technologies, and Germany is bolstering Ukraine with IRIS-T systems and thousands of drones. How Russia's military and economic systems are buckling simultaneously — in this issue.

recentItems.title: The Kremlin FABRICATES 70% for "United Russia" on the ruins of occupied cities
recentItems.description:
Russia is preparing for State Duma elections, yet virtually no real political competition remains. The opposition is barred from the race, candidates avoid debates, and criticizing Putin, the authorities, or the consequences of the war is effectively prohibited. The Kremlin also plans to conduct illegal voting in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine with pre-determined outcomes. Meanwhile, within Russia itself, fear of a new wave of mobilization is rising, with citizens increasingly searching for information on conscription and ways to flee the country.

Meanwhile, Moscow persists with air attacks despite US diplomatic efforts and the visit of Witkoff and Kushner. Experts emphasize: a real path to peace requires stronger sanctions, enhanced Ukrainian air defense, and relentless pressure on Russia's military-economic capabilities.

recentItems.title: Is Ukraine preparing a surprise for the Kremlin? Superdrones with Starlink could attack soon
recentItems.description:
Russia is considering scenarios for a new offensive on Kyiv and Chernihiv, but Ukraine is already preparing a multi-layered defense of its northern border. Meanwhile, Kyiv may gain new capabilities for its drones thanks to Starlink, which could significantly expand their effectiveness. Another crucial direction is the production of Storm Shadow missiles inside Ukraine and strikes on Russian command posts in Donetsk. The Ukrainian defense industry is scaling up cooperation with Europe, securing new "drone deals," and acquiring technologies for missiles and air defense.

recentItems.title: Ukraine offers CEASEFIRE — Russia ANSWERS with STRIKES during US VISIT
recentItems.description:
Russia continues massive attacks on Ukraine despite talks of a potential air truce: overnight, Russian forces deployed ballistic missiles and 167 drones. Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia, and the Dnipropetrovsk region came under strike. At the same time, the Defense Forces refute Moscow's claims of new territorial gains and are conducting counterattacks, particularly in the Kupiansk area. Meanwhile, Germany closes the Russian Consulate General in Bonn amid suspicions of intelligence and hybrid activity, and Lithuania strengthens its airspace control system.
